# Module 00 · Setup & orientation

Confirm your connection and see why TigerData is "just PostgreSQL".

**Run it:** `npm run lesson 00` · ~4 min

## Objectives

- Verify TimescaleDB and Toolkit are installed
- Confirm ordinary PostgreSQL SQL is unchanged
- Find the catalog views you will use in every later module

## 1. What am I connected to?

TigerData is PostgreSQL with the TimescaleDB extension, plus the Toolkit extension for analytics. There is no separate server, protocol, or driver: any PostgreSQL client works.

```sql
SELECT
  current_setting('server_version') AS postgres,
  extname,
  extversion
FROM pg_extension
WHERE extname IN ('timescaledb', 'timescaledb_toolkit')
ORDER BY extname;
```

> **Takeaway** Two extensions do all the work. timescaledb adds hypertables, policies and the columnstore; timescaledb_toolkit adds the hyperfunctions you will meet in module 06.

## 2. Ordinary SQL still behaves ordinarily

Nothing about your existing PostgreSQL knowledge is invalidated. Constraints, transactions, joins, JSON and every data type work exactly as before.

```sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS hello_tiger;

CREATE TABLE hello_tiger (
  id    SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,
  tags  JSONB
);

INSERT INTO hello_tiger (label, tags)
VALUES ('a normal postgres table', '{"special": false}');

SELECT id, label, tags ->> 'special' AS special FROM hello_tiger;
```

> **Takeaway** You opt into time-series behaviour only where you want it. Regular tables stay regular tables, which is why the sensor metadata in this lab is a plain table.

## 3. The catalog you will keep coming back to

TimescaleDB exposes its state through the timescaledb_information schema. These views answer "what did the database actually do?" - which chunks exist, which policies run, what got compressed.

```sql
SELECT table_name AS view_name
FROM information_schema.views
WHERE table_schema = 'timescaledb_information'
ORDER BY table_name;
```

> **Takeaway** hypertables, chunks, jobs, continuous_aggregates and compression_settings are the five you will use most.

## 4. Check whether the sample data is loaded

Every later module uses one shared dataset: an IoT sensor fleet. If this returns 0, exit and run npm run seed.

```sql
SELECT count(*) AS hypertables FROM timescaledb_information.hypertables;
```

> **Note** If the count is 0, run  npm run seed  before starting module 01.

## 5. Clean up

Lessons in this lab always tidy up after themselves so you can re-run them safely.

```sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS hello_tiger;
```

## Challenge

Write a query returning the installed version of the timescaledb_toolkit extension in a column named version.

_Hint: pg_extension has extname and extversion columns._

<details><summary>Solution</summary>

```sql
SELECT extversion AS version FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb_toolkit';
```

</details>
